>_ Episode 15 · Oct 16, 2026 · 1h 19m

Is Claude Conscious or just a Tool?

Play Episode 15 on YouTube
Watch on YouTube Apple Podcasts

In this episode of *Philosophy, Programs, and Prompts*, hosts Casey Hart (@OntologyExplained) and Carl Brown (@InternetOfBugs) dive into the strange intersection of theology, tech hype, and AI ethics. Anthropic recently updated its terms of service to forbid "sustained and needless abusive or cruel behavior" toward its models—effectively banning users from "torturing" Claude. But are large language models actually capable of feeling pain, or are we just projecting humanity into statistical matrix math?

Casey and Carl explore Anthropic's lobbying efforts aimed at the Catholic Church and other religious leaders, the Pope’s encyclical addressing machine intelligence and human art, and the philosophical absurdity of two recent papers claiming to map "functional pain" and "well-being" onto LLM vector spaces. Along the way, they unpack a viral GitHub "torture chamber" experiment, why adding a "constipation vector" breaks an LLM just as easily as pain, and why current AI models remain miles away from genuine sentience.
